llm_explanation: The time series displays a single, powerful transient event with a very rapid rise and decay, lasting approximately 50-60 days. This fast evolution is much quicker than typical supernovae (like SNIa or SNII) and is a defining characteristic of a kilonova (KN), which is powered by the radioactive decay of r-process elements following a compact object merger. The object is also observed to be brighter in bluer/greener wavelengths at its peak, consistent with the hot initial phase of a KN before it rapidly cools and reddens. The long period of quiescence followed by a single, fast outburst further supports its classification as a rare explosive transient rather than a variable star or AGN.

The event shows a very high peak luminosity, as indicated by the high flux values, and a long duration with a slow rise of approximately 50-60 days to maximum light followed by a similarly slow decline.
